newsitem.title: USA: MCI signs key U.S. wireless strategy pact.
newsitem.headline: MCI signs key U.S. wireless strategy pact.

text.p: MCI Communications Corp said Monday it had agreed to a large-scale, 10-year wireless resale pact with NextWave Telecom Inc which thrusts MCI into the first league of U.S. wireless communications providers.

Under terms of the deal, MCI said it will connect its intelligent network to NextWave's planned national Personal Communications Services system, securing the capacity to offer PCS service to more than 110 million individuals in 63 markets, including 29 of the top 50 markets.
MCI said it will buy at least 10 billion minutes of PCS capacity from NextWave over 10 years.

The deal will help underpin the financial future of debt-laden NextWave, which was the largest bidder in the U.S. Federal Communications Commission auctions for "C-band" wireless radio spectrum held in early July.
The company, which has filed to hold its initial public offering, will trade under the symbol "SURF" on the Nasdaq.
For MCI the deal allows it to expand rapidly into the rapidly growing market for wireless personal communications services (PCS).
Two years ago, MCI dropped out of the auctions for U.S. PCS licences after the bidding became too rich for its tastes.
But with the NextWave pact and previous smaller deals MCI has moved to become a major reseller of wireless services.
As part of the deal, NextWave has selected MCI to provide telecommunications and other services supporting the development and ongoing operations of its PCS system, MCI said.

"This agreement with NextWave establishes an immediate nationwide PCS footprint for MCI and represents an important next step in MCI's wireless strategy," said Whitey Bluestein, vice president, MCI wireless strategy and development.

"This is the first full interconnection agreement of its kind and brings new competition to the wireless marketplace," he said, noting that with full interconnection, MCI does not need to own its own wireless facilities.
MCI said the NextWave agreement is a model for additional agreements it expects to sign with other wireless providers as part of its Wireless Interconnected Network (WIN) strategy.

The strategy is MCI's blueprint for building a national wireless footprint that allows it to offer a full range of wireless services and features that are fully integrated into MCI's existing suite of communications services.
"This was MCI's strategy all along," said Jeffrey Kagan, an Atlanta-based telecommunications industry analyst.

Kagan said MCI has historically preferred to resell communications services initially rather than investing in their own infrastructure. Over time, the company selectively builds its own infrastructure as it is proven profitable to do so.

"Reselling service was how they became a heavy hitter in long distance in the first place," Kagan said. "What their plan is is to resell service from other providers and build networks where they see the need to do so," he said.
Still, Kagan said MCI's deal with NextWave marks the rapid realization of its reseller strategy. "This all of a sudden puts MCI on the wireless communications map in a big way."

Still, he noted that AT&T Corp's AT&T Wireless unit, the former McCaw Cellular business, remains twice as large as MCI's cellular business, with about 6.5 million subscribers in geographic regions covering 207 million potential customers.
MCI's deal with NextWave covers about 110 million potential customers living in a mix of metropolitan and less densely populated areas of the United States.
NextWave is based in San Diego and New York.
-- Eric Auchard, New York Newsdesk, 212-859-1736
